device.name: Space Robotics Bench _manipulation template (Isaac Sim Gymnasium environment)

facts.text: Space Robotics Bench is a collection of environments and tasks for robotics research in space, providing a unified framework
The simulation runs on NVIDIA Isaac Sim
The CLI refuses to run without the omni module, requiring an environment with NVIDIA Omniverse and Isaac Sim installed
The CLI creates an environment with gymnasium.make(id=env_id, cfg=env_cfg, render_mode=...)
register_srb_tasks registers each task with gymnasium.register under the default namespace srb as f'{namespace}/{id}'
The manipulation template registers its package name and a _visual variant with Task as default_entry_point and TaskCfg as default_task_cfg
The docs list _manipulation as a barebones template whose entry point is Task(ManipulationEnv) and whose config is TaskCfg(ManipulationEnvCfg)
The docs invoke the template with 'srb agent rand -e _manipulation ...'
The template environment class is Task(ManipulationEnv), constructed from a TaskCfg
TaskCfg sets episode_length_s to 10.0 and is_finite_horizon to False
truncate_episodes defaults to True
The manipulation env runs physics at env_rate 1/150 s and the agent at agent_rate 1/50 s
The cfg sets decimation to floor(agent_rate / env_rate) and sim.dt to env_rate
The default robot of ManipulationEnvCfg is Franka
The default Franka action group is a differential inverse-kinematics relative pose command with command_type pose, use_relative_mode True and scale 0.1
The default Franka action addresses joints panda_joint1 through panda_joint7
The action space is a Box with low -1.0 and high 1.0 per element, shaped by action_manager.total_action_dim
The observation is a Dict with the groups state, state_dyn, proprio and proprio_dyn
The proprio group carries the end-effector position and its 6D rotation, and proprio_dyn carries the normalized robot and end-effector joint positions
The end-effector rotation is converted to a 6D representation with rotmat_to_rot6d
The reward sums four penalty terms: action rate, joint torque, joint acceleration and undesired robot contacts
The action-rate penalty is -0.5 times the mean squared difference between the current and previous action
There is no termination condition; the episode is truncated when the episode length reaches max_episode_length if truncate_episodes is true
The reset randomizes the robot joints with a uniform position offset of +-5 degrees and a zero velocity range
DirectEnv imports DirectRLEnv from isaaclab.envs, so the Gymnasium reset and step implementations come from outside the clone
DirectEnv.close deletes the action manager and closes the Isaac Lab environment

determinism.notes: the fake reseeds Python's random.Random from reset(seed) or cap.world.seed.v1 and its kinematic update is deterministic, so one seed repeats a trajectory; the upstream seed is a scenario seed consumed by Isaac Sim, and the fake was not compared with it

gaps: kinematic F0 stand-in with no rigid-body dynamics, contacts, friction, actuator, sensor or noise model; only the action-rate reward term is reproduced, so its trajectories are not Isaac Sim's

the upstream simulation path (gymnasium.make('srb/_manipulation')) needs Python 3.11, NVIDIA Omniverse and Isaac Sim (srb/__main__.py:37-40) and was never opened here; only the package fake backend is exercised

the fake returns only the proprio and proprio_dyn observation groups, each one vector of its members in sorted name order as the upstream concatenates them (srb/core/env/common/base/direct/impl.py:543-556): a constant 3D position and a constant 6D rotation, and a two-joint hand vector before a seven-joint arm vector; the upstream observation also has the state and state_dyn contact-force groups, and all fake observation values are placeholder test data

the fake action Box has the seven elements of action_manager.total_action_dim in the default configuration (the Franka's six relative pose values and its hand's binary gripper value), while another robot, tool or action group changes the upstream width at run time; the fake adds the pose values to its arm joints without inverse kinematics and sets the hand joints to the gripper's close or open command at once, without the hand's actuator
the fake truncates at 500 agent steps (10 s at 50 Hz), an approximation of the max_episode_length Isaac Lab computes from the cfg; no termination condition is modelled
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0 and clock lockstep, so ticks advance simulated time by timestep_ms only
snapshots and restore are not offered: the environment exposes no get_state/set_state
the fake was never compared with an Isaac Sim run, and no simulator or hardware evidence exists

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
